_what_this_is: A POST-SEARCH / PRE-BEHAVIOUR protocol decision. The formal search is complete and no behavioural recovery result has been observed, so this is not outcome-driven candidate selection. It derives the behavioural screening set prospectively from the already-completed 12-leaf ranking under a new standing retention rule.
_authorizes: nothing. Behavioural screening is a separately authorized session.

the_standing_policy.rule: Diversity is used only during search-time beam pruning. Final post-search Top-K must NOT use lineage diversity.
the_standing_policy.scope: D1/D2/D3 and all future full-search experiments, across Stage 0-6, model sizes, compression ratios, operator spaces and model families. The objectives may differ per experiment; the structural rule does not.
the_standing_policy.why: During a search a state is a PARTIAL hypothesis, and one early proxy measurement must not extinguish an entire structural family -- so beam pruning keeps a slot per lineage. Once complete leaves exist that job is finished. The remaining question is only which complete candidates the search objectives themselves rank highest.
the_standing_policy.search_time: epsilon-Pareto quality + lineage diversity -> preserve exploration
the_standing_policy.post_search: epsilon-Pareto quality order + deterministic tie-break -> NO lineage diversity
the_standing_policy._not_a_new_scalar_score: the three objectives and the epsilon are unchanged. Quality order means: compute the epsilon-Pareto fronts, order them best to worst, use the policy's deterministic tie-break inside each front, concatenate, take the first K. It is NOT a sort by equal_domain_mean or by any single objective -- collapsing a multi-objective search into one number is the failure the fronts exist to prevent.
the_standing_policy._if_diversity_after_recovery_is_wanted: it must be declared as a separate scientific objective or experiment, not inherited implicitly from the beam's exploration policy.

what_prompted_it.finding: the search's Stage D reused the beam's retention rule, so the committed Top-4 was not the four best complete leaves. The policy rotates over operator-order lineages, keeping one state per lineage before any lineage gets a second.

the_fourth_committed_finalist.why_it_was_in: the only width-first lineage that produced a complete leaf
the_fourth_committed_finalist.worse_than: seven leaves that were not committed

what_prompted_it._so: retention WIDTH and retention CRITERION are independent choices. Widening Top-2 to Top-4 did not change the criterion, and the two candidates it was adopted to admit were exactly the ones it still excluded.

the_frozen_behavioural_finalists.derived_from: logs/stages/stage-1/phase_d1/runs/d1_search_20261006_210210/evidence/complete_leaf_ranking.json -- the completed search's own 12-leaf ranking, unmodified
the_frozen_behavioural_finalists._derivation_is_checked: the first four of the completed search's quality order equal this set exactly; the equality is asserted rather than asserted-by-hand.

Adoption still compares against that record rather than against this file, but a decision document carrying truncated identities would be a trap for anyone who read it as authoritative.

what_is_NOT_being_rewritten.the_completed_search: d1_search_20261006_210210 remains valid and accepted. It is NOT rerun. Its Stage-D selection -- quality positions 1, 3, 5 and 11 -- remains the historical record of what its own policy committed, unmodified, in its closeout and in stage1_selection.json.
what_is_NOT_being_rewritten.the_search_semantics: beam width 6, one warmup level, the epsilon-Pareto objectives, lineage diversity DURING beam pruning, K=200 reference_topk_tail_v1, bsz=3, length_sorted_v1, the operator space, both calibration profiles, the supervised_target position policy and the state-eval semantics are all unchanged. The search used diversity correctly for exploration.
what_is_NOT_being_rewritten.phase_b_and_c2: their historical final selections used the same lineage-diverse policy and their evidence remains valid under the protocol they actually ran. They are NOT revised and NOT called invalid -- they answered a different candidate-selection protocol. Nor should their Top-K be described as 'the best K by proxy score': it was not, and under lineage rotation it never was.

consequences.rematerialization_contract: from the committed search records, using the recorded operator implementations, operator order, calibration profiles, target geometry, teacher/tokenizer/input identities and frozen execution configuration. Adoption requires EXACT equality on artifact_digest, weights_digest, single_shard_sha256 and arch_signature. An approximately equivalent checkpoint is not substituted, and no core identity check is weakened; a mismatch is a deterministic-materialization defect to diagnose.
consequences.retirement_contract: heavy checkpoint bytes only, and only once #2 and #4 are secured and identity-verified. Their measurement, ranking position, operator path, every digest, manifest and provenance are RETAINED. Both remain in the 12-leaf ranking as the leaves they are; what goes is weight bytes with no remaining downstream consumer.
consequences.screening: 4 candidate initializations x 2 screening seeds = 8 probes, plus incumbent B x 2 matched seeds = 2, for 10 screening probes. Then exactly one advancing candidate, then 3 fresh confirmation seeds against B on matched seeds. Candidate membership does not change after screening begins.

implementation.generic_mechanism: aadistill.initialization.planning.ranking -- `BeamRankingPolicy.quality_order()` is the one shared epsilon-Pareto ordering; `rank(..., diversity=False)` and `SearchResult.finalists(policy, k)` are the quality-only retention path. PARETO_V1 is unchanged and beam pruning keeps its diversity, so every existing search behaves exactly as before.
implementation.no_experiment_hardcode_in_core: no phase id, no model name or geometry, no stage id, no K, no candidate id. K and the choice of quality-only retention belong to experiment configuration.
implementation.d1_wiring: the D1 driver's Stage D now commits via `result.finalists(PARETO_V1, k)`, so a future D1-family search retains by quality order natively.
implementation.hash_bound: `behavioural_design.finalist_retention` is part of the design's scientific preimage, so changing the retention rule moves the scientific design hash.
